history.summary: An ancient shrine at the foot of Mount Girnar whose origins lie in the Puranic era; the lingam is held to be svayambhu (self-manifested). Legend says that as Shiva and Parvati crossed the Girnar hills their divine garment fell at the Mrigi Kund, making it a holy Shaivite site; to this day Naga sadhus bathe in Mrigi Kund before joining the Maha Shivratri procession. The precise founding is unknown - the fair itself is of great antiquity. The five-day Bhavnath fair in the Magha month (February-March), culminating at midnight on Maha Shivratri with the Dashanami Naga sadhus, and the Girnar Lili Parikrama are the two main annual events. name: Bhavnath Mahadev Temple
town_description: Junagadh is a city at the foot of the Girnar hills in the Saurashtra region of Gujarat, once the capital of the former princely state of Junagadh. It is known for the Ashokan rock edicts (c. 250 BCE), the Uparkot fort and the Mahabat Maqbara, and is the gateway for pilgrims climbing Mount Girnar and visitors to Sasan Gir. The district headquarters is a major religious-tourism hub of western Gujarat.

travel.road: Bhavnath locality at Girnar Taleti, ~5 km from Junagadh city centre; starting point of the Girnar climb

visitor_information.best_time: October to March; Maha Shivratri (February-March) is the peak pilgrimage time
